text:
Anna (customer): Hi team, we started seeing streaming responses truncate after a long idle period. Client gets a partial last chunk, then reconnects and ends up with duplicated tokens. Happening through our ALB -> nginx -> app chain. Logs attached.
Sam (support): Sorry about that — can you paste a minimal repro curl + headers and approximate timings? Also which edge (Cloudflare/none)?
Anna (customer): Repro: our client does long poll-ish streaming. Example curl we used:\n\n```
curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=redwood-xx&stream=true"
```
Server sends first event immediately, then sleeps ~35s, then sends the rest. Observed truncation around 33-36s. Edge is Cloudflare in front of ALB.
Lee (infra-oncall): Quick checklist: ALB idle timeout default is 60s, but Cloudflare and nginx buffering can reorder flushes. Do you have nginx `proxy_buffering` on? Also check `proxy_read_timeout` / `proxy_send_timeout` and `proxy_http_version` (1.1 needed for chunked flushes).
Maya (dev): Our node/express handler does: `res.write("data: partial\n\n"); await sleep(35000); res.write("data: rest\n\n"); res.end();` — no Content-Length, chunked by default. We assumed flush happens immediately but maybe nginx buffered it.
Paul (eng-runtime): Common cause: intermediate proxy buffers small chunks until buffer fills or timeout. nginx default `proxy_buffering on` will buffer unless `proxy_buffering off;` or `proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Connection "";` + `proxy_set_header Transfer-Encoding ""` depending on config. Cloudflare will also buffer responses for certain content-types unless using their "disable buffering" or passing `Cache-Control: no-transform` / `Content-Type: text/event-stream` and proper SSE semantics. Also check ALB idle timeout vs keepalives on targets.
Sam (support): Can you share nginx location block? Also any tcp logs showing FIN or RST around the truncate? Deploy-bot shows recent deploys: `deploy-bot: deployment/api-stream v2026.03.15` (no obvious changes since).
Anna (customer): Nginx conf excerpt: \n```
location /v1/stream/ {
  proxy_pass http://upstream;
  proxy_http_version 1.1;
  proxy_set_header Connection "";
  proxy_buffering on;   # default
  proxy_read_timeout 60s;
}
```
We didn't set proxy_buffering off.
Lee (infra-oncall): Try this quick workaround: set `proxy_buffering off;` and `proxy_send_timeout 90s; proxy_read_timeout 90s;` for the stream path and add SSE heartbeats from the app every 15s. Heartbeat example: `res.write(': hb\n\n');` — keeps proxies from considering connection idle.
Maya (dev): Added heartbeat and set `proxy_buffering off` in a staging flip. Repro run: much better, no truncation after 40s. Client still reconnects sometimes but without duplicate tokens now. Logs show no upstream EOF at that time.
Paul (eng-runtime): Additional recommendations: ensure responses are `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` (no Content-Length), disable `sendfile` if using open_file optimizations that may interfere with flushes, and on ALB increase idle timeout to 120s for streaming targets. For Cloudflare, if you can't disable buffering globally, use a Cloudflare Page Rule / Worker to pass through SSE or use the Stream service.
Sam (support): For completeness, capture tcpdump or `nginx -V` and `curl -v --no-buffer` output if it recurs. Also collect request id from our tracing header `x-rw-trace-id` so we can correlate.
Anna (customer): Thanks — changed config and pushed heartbeat. Staging run looks good. I'll keep an eye and open a ticket for us to roll the change to prod after some canary runs (#SUP-7892). :thumbsup:
Lee (infra-oncall): Nice. If it recurs after the changes, please attach `nginx error.log` + the ALB target health logs + Cloudflare request id. We can also add an automated canary that exercises a 45s delayed chunk path.
Paul (eng-runtime): One more note: if you see partial bytes without proper chunk boundaries, client libs sometimes treat that as a closed stream. For lib-level robustness, recommend client to treat reconnects idempotently and dedupe tokens using server-side id or sequence numbers in the stream events.
Anna (customer): Will do. Appreciate the quick triage everyone.
Maya (dev): Filing follow-up PR for `proxy_buffering off` + docs entry about SSE caveats: `docs/streaming-ops.md`.
Sam (support): Closing triage here, moving to ticket tracking. Ping if anything else pops up.
